title: Microburst Wrangler — personal design log
text:
Context / goal:
- Short log / scratchpad for a small, pragmatic approach to handling microbursts at the ingress layer (10s-100s reqs/sec spiky bursts per tenant) without blowing up downstream GPU queues or massively increasing tail latency.
- Keep this lightweight: a tunable "microburst wrangler" that composes admission, cheap sampling, and adaptive prefilling/warmup.

Key constraints we care about:
- Per-tenant fairness: avoid a single tenant saturating slot pool.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 300ms for interactive routes, p99 < 800ms target.
- Cost: minimal additional CPU/Memory; rely on existing ingress proxies.

Proposed components (sketch):
1) Fast-path admission gate (stateless-ish): token-bucket per-tenant + short-term burst buffer counter. Reject -> enqueue to slow-lane if configured.
2) Burst-sample profiler: sample ~1% of requests in a burst window, run light-weight predictor (linear model) to estimate expected tokens/seq-len + likelihood of multi-turn continuation.
3) Prefill/warmup trigger: for requests that pass predictor threshold, emit prewarm signal to runner cluster for that (tenant, model-variant) key (TTL short).
4) Slow-lane queue: short in-memory bounded queue per-affinity zone. Use backpressure/backoff hints to callers (503 + Retry-After or graceful degrade responses).

ASCII flow:
  client -> ingress -> admission gate -> [allowed] -> runner -> model
                                    
                              -> [sample profiler] -> prewarm signal -> runner cache
                              -> [slow-lane enqueue] -> dequeue -> runner

Operational heuristics to tune (initial defaults):
- burst_threshold_window = 2s
- bucket_capacity = 50 tokens (one token ~= 1 request unit)
- allowed_burst_multiplier = 4
- sample_rate_during_burst = 0.01 (1%)
- prewarm_ttl = 1.5s
- slow_lane_max_len = 200 reqs per zone

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Where to place predictor? ingress side adds CPU cost but reduces wasted GPU prewarm signals. Could push to separate profiling service.
- How to measure "benefit" of prewarm reliably? We need per-prefill telemetry tying prewarm -> reduced cold-start tokens and end-to-end latency improvements.
- Interaction with dedicated capacity pools: should dedicated tenants bypass slow-lane? likely if capacity reserved.
- Security/tenancy: keep prewarm signals tenant-scoped and authenticated to avoid cross-tenant leakage.

Small experiment plan:
- Sim sim harness (first pass): replay traces (from ENG-5421) with injected synthetic bursts (1s, 3s, 10s) and compare metrics: p95/p99, queue drops, GPU utilization.
- Implement a lightweight admission gate in the ingress test harness that supports sampling and prewarm signals; measure false-positive prewarm ratio.
- Measure overhead of predictor at 10k reqs/s (cpu) in a small k8s pod.

Quick TODOs (near-term):
- [ ] write a quick simulator (python) that runs per-tenant Poisson + burst overlay and runs above heuristics (target: 2 dev-days).
- [ ] add telemetry tags: prewarm_triggered, prewarm_hit, slow_lane_enqueue, slow_lane_dequeue, admission_reject_reason.
- [ ] prototype predictor model: features = seq_len_estimate, recent-turns, tenant_qos_tier, route_hint; model = small logistic regression for "long running" or "likely continuation".
- [ ] sync with SRE on backpressure semantics and retry guidance for clients.

Notes to self:
- Keep admission gate configable by route (console) — product wants per-route controls.
- Consider exposing "burst budget" UI in Console -> per-route chart: active bursts, refill rate, current tokens.
- When in doubt, prefer graceful degradation (short informative response) over silently dropping requests.

Rough sim output snapshot (toy run):
- baseline (no wrangler): p95=360ms p99=1140ms, gpu_util=78%, dropped=0
- wrangler v0 (simple bucket + slow-lane): p95=280ms p99=610ms, gpu_util=66%, dropped=1.7%
- wrangler v1 (add prewarm profiler): p95=240ms p99=520ms, gpu_util=64%, dropped=1.6%, prewarm_hit_rate=0.42

End — this is intentionally messy. Next session: flesh out simulator parameters and share short RFC sketch with eng-serving-runtime and SRE.

References/links (for follow-up):
- ENG-5421 trace dump (linked above)
- runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1689 (prefill hooks)
- prior notes: #ingress-burst-sim slack thread (search)

-- Priya
